summary: Instagram is where almost all the audience is: most Hindi videos get 500 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly stay under 100 views. The best videos name a familiar gadget or robot and add a surprising twist, like 'it doesn't see, it only senses heat'. Early October videos with plain 'How does X work?' titles got almost nothing on Instagram, and some were never posted there at all.
winningPattern: Surprising 'X doesn't do the obvious thing, it actually does Y' framing about a relatable gadget or maker module (robot, clap switch, DHT11, mic, breathalyzer). Hindi titles in Hinglish with a 'Nahi... sirf...' contrast and an emoji, posted on Instagram. Robot and clap-switch topics get the most views and saves; myth-busting about everyday experiences (UV in clouds, sunburn) gets the most shares. Generic 'Kaise kaam karta hai? 🤔' question titles and YouTube-only posts perform worst.
doMore: Post every video to Instagram Reels too, since YouTube-only uploads got almost no views
Use the 'doesn't do X, only does Y' hook with a robot or a familiar gadget
Make myth-busting videos about daily experiences (sunburn, cloudy days, safety) to earn shares
End with a practical tip or a diagram worth saving, as the robot and clap switch videos got the most saves
Make short series on the winning topics, like robot sensors and sound switches, with each video using a new angle
stopDoing: Generic 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai? 🤔' titles with no surprising claim
Publishing videos to only one platform
Repeating near-identical topics (clap switch, IR sensor) without a new angle
